result.rationale:
The diff confirms zoho-bigin's CalendarService passes `credentialId` as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens (`"zoho-bigin",
 credentialId`), unlike every other call site (googlecalendar, hubspot, webex, etc.) which passes `credential.userId`. Since refreshOAuthTokens puts that value into `calcomUserId` in the sync request, a credential row id would be sent as the user id; and being non-null, the `userId` guard that falls back to direct refresh won't catch it. Verified mechanism, real defect.

judged_text: The zoho-bigin refresh passes `credentialId` — not `credential.userId`, as every other call site in this diff does — as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, so the credential row id lands in the calcomUserId request field. In sync mode the parent application receives a credential id where the contract defines the user id, so it resolves the wrong user (or none) and either fails the sync or attaches the wrong account's credentials; because the value is non-null, the null-guard that routes team credentials to the direct refresh cannot catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is `userId` and, in sync mode, it is sent as `calcomUserId` (`userId.toString()`) to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Every other updated call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`, so this one will send a credential row id (or at least a non-user id) where a user id is expected, leading to incorrect/failed sync and bypassing the `userId` null-guard.
